Subject: Renewal inquiry — right-sizing commit and uplift guardrails

Hi Sean,

Our annual renewal is coming up for the hosted API contract (current commit ~1.0B tokens/year). Before we finalize internal approvals, procurement asked us to see if Redwood can: 

- Propose a right-sized commit option (we're targeting ~700M tokens/year) with tiered per-token pricing.
- Offer a cap on annual uplift (we want predictability — initial ask is a 20% uplift cap year-over-year).
- Provide a mid-year true-up window and a mechanism for credits if usage falls below the committed amount.

Can you send a short written proposal with a couple of priced options and any constraints we should be aware of? We need something to share with finance by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Jamie

Head of Platform Procurement
Acme Corp

Hi Jamie — appreciate the clear ask.

We can absolutely put together two clean options for Acme that balance predictability and unit economics. High level (we'll send a formal PDF):

Option A — Right-size + standard discount
- Commit: 700M tokens/year
- Per-token: $0.00095 (10% off list)
- Annual uplift cap: 20%
- True-up window: quarterly true-up with 30-day settlement
- No make-good credit for unused commit (standard T&Cs)

Option B — Flex-credit program (recommended for variability)
- Commit: 800M tokens/year (smoothed price)
- Per-token: $0.00088 (15% off list)
- Flex credits: unused tokens in a quarter convert to credits redeemable in next two quarters (up to 15% of quarter commit)
- Annual uplift cap: 25%
- One-time onboarding credit if you sign by Dec 15: $10k

I'll attach a formal proposal PDF with explicit pricing grids and SLA appendix. Looping in Alex (pricing) and Lauren (sales leader) to finalize internal okays.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday to walk through?

Best,

FYI — Jamie asked for a short written proposal. Draft included below; highlights and questions for you both: 

Proposal highlights I want to present to Acme:
- Offer two clean lanes: 700M (lower commit, smaller discount) and 800M (higher commit + flex-credit).
- Flex-credit mechanics: unused tokens (by quarter) convert 1:1 to credit usable in next two quarters up to 15% of quarter commit. Credits expire after those two quarters.
- Uplift cap: 20% vs 25% tradeoff (lower cap = smaller discount).
- One-time onboarding credit of $10k for an early-sign.

Questions / constraints:
1) Alex — finance: can we allow credits that expire after two quarters without creating revenue recognition headaches? If not, propose a one-time make-good credit equal to 50% of unused commit value (instead of rolling credits).
2) Lauren — sales leadership: are we comfortable capping uplift at 25% for year-one only, then 20% thereafter? I want to avoid long-term exposure.

If you both ok, I'll send Option A/B to Jamie with the attached PDF and DocuSign link for the 800M flex option.

Thanks,
Sean

Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme renewal — draft pricing options (need sign-off)

Thanks for the draft, Sean. A few points from finance/legal: 

- Flex credits that expire within two quarters are doable, but we need explicit accounting language in the SOW: credits are liabilities until consumed; we'll require a 12-month lookback for audit purposes. Finance asks we cap outstanding credit liability at 15% of annual commit (that aligns with the proposed 15% per-quarter cap).
- Alternative (lower risk): a one-time make-good credit equal to 40% of the dollar value of unused commit for the first year only. That's simpler to book and easier for our CS ops team.
- Uplift cap: legal ok with 25% for year-one if we include a staged cap (25% year-one, 20% year-two). No more than 20% thereafter.
- Pricing tweak: if Acme accepts 800M + flex-credit, can we set per-token to $0.00087 (trim 1c) to keep rounding simple?

I recommend we present both: (1) Flex-credit with accounting language, 800M @ $0.00087, 25% YoY cap Y1/20% Y2; (2) Simpler: 700M @ $0.00095 with 20% cap and make-good credit (40% unused $ value).

Also add HubSpot deal link in the PDF and include SLA appendix (redwood-sla-appendix.pdf).

-Alex

Jamie — thanks for the convo this week. Per our discussion and internal approvals, here are two final options for Acme to review: 

Option 1 — Predictable Right-Size
- Commit: 700M tokens/year
- Per-token: $0.00095
- Annual uplift cap: 20% YoY
- True-up: quarterly true-up; settlement within 30 days
- Make-good: if annual usage < commit, Acme receives a make-good credit equal to 40% of the dollar value of unused tokens for the first contract year; credit applies against future usage.

Option 2 — Flex-Credit (recommended for variable workloads)
- Commit: 800M tokens/year
- Per-token: $0.00087
- Flex credits: unused tokens in any quarter convert 1:1 to credits redeemable in the next two quarters, capped at 15% of quarter commit. Credits expire after two quarters.
- Accounting guardrail: outstanding credits capped at 15% of annual commit as a liability (per finance requirement).
- Annual uplift cap: 25% YoY in year 1, 20% YoY in year 2+
- One-time early-sign credit: $10,000 if signed by Dec 15
